attachment_note: Both attached PNGs were opened with Read at native 1400x900 and judged directly as images. No SVG was opened, read, listed, searched, rendered or git-shown, and no image other than the two named PNGs was opened; crops written to the run's /tmp scratch directory are magnifications of those same PNGs, not new renders. Mapping by content: image-0 carries an X-point magnified window, which only the diverted state has (its analytic saddle is the only non-None saddle in the renderer), so it is the diverted trial panel; image-1 carries an axis-only window, the limited trial panel. Provenance: the reviewed head's fragment docs/evidence/fragments/sub-millisecond-forward-path/tracked-read-h200.html:178-194 binds each img src to one of the two SVG paths; the figure blobs and the renderer (blob at scripts/prototypes/tracked_read_h200/figures.py calling _render_read_panel in tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py) are unchanged between 15f6cfddf and this head (git diff empty), so this is the same artwork the figure review at 15f6cfddf judged, re-rendered at 14x9 in at 100 dpi.

findings.summary: Both magnified null windows keep a full four-spine grey frame: lines 940-942 only recolour each spine (#888888, lw 1.2) and never remove the top and right spines, so each window reads as a boxed sub-plot where the repository's data-ink rule despines every axis. Visible on both the diverted panel (two windows) and the limited panel (one window). Non-blocking: the frames are thin and do not obscure the marks; the axes and ticks are already off.

The normal-form boundary contour is drawn solid in the cell-field feature colour (levels[:1], DEFAULT_INK.flux_color, linewidth 2.6) while the legend reads 'cell field / dashed', so a prominent solid blue line is not covered by the legend vocabulary and a reader can take it for an unlabelled third series. Visible on the diverted panel where the boundary contour is drawn. Non-blocking: the caption names the solid analytic versus dashed cell-field vocabulary and the mark remains identifiable by colour.
